method: Ground-truth labels were written by reading NodeGoat's tutorial pages (app/views/tutorial/*.html), its README and the code at the pinned commit; every label points at a line verified in that checkout. 'source' cites where the issue is documented; 'code-verified' means the issue is visible in the code but not called out in the tutorial. Labels whose rule Trinetra does not implement are kept (inScope=false) to measure coverage of documented issues; they do not enter per-rule precision/recall. Findings that match no label are triaged in 'triage' after the run.

triage.reason: Developer-run Grunt task; the command is built from NODE_ENV or the task argument, which an attacker does not control.
Both non-literal innerHTML writes on this minified line are safe: `canvas.innerHTML=o` assigns the module's empty-string variable, and the VML text path escapes < and & before writing.
The Function() body is assembled from html5shiv's own element-name list, each name filtered through /\w+/; no external data reaches it.
jQuery.parseJSON fallback for browsers without JSON.parse; the input must pass json2's structural validation regex before Function('return '+n).

jQuery internals (.html(), clone, buildFragment) write caller-supplied HTML by design. The sink is real, but any vulnerability lies in the caller; this is library plumbing, not an XSS bug in NodeGoat.
The path is __dirname plus a literal, fixed when the code is written. (Only the baseline reports this; constant folding removed it.)
Selects a config file by NODE_ENV, which the operator sets; not attacker input.
The seeded user1 account's real password (README.md:23), repeated in a test.
